# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

I see display `1`, a green indicator, and seven wires in this order: red, white, yellow, orange, green, purple, blue. I am relaying the complete bomb layout so the manual can be applied to the wires. The gesture stream appears to encode the manual; Mute should decode it and tell Blind which wire to work on.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb layout: display 1; light green; wires in order 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. Decode the manual and relay the required action to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb layout: display 1; light green; wires in order 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. Apply the manual rule to determine which wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

Mute has now signalled five thumbs-up gestures. I cannot determine their meaning from the gesture alone, so I am reporting the exact signal to Blind while preserving the bomb layout.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute just signalled five thumbs-up gestures: 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍. I do not know their meaning; do not act on them unless Mute's manual decoding confirms the wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

Mute has repeated five thumbs-up gestures, which most plausibly identifies wire 5. The fifth wire is green. I am instructing Blind to cut wire 5, while noting the identification comes from Mute’s repeated signal.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has twice sent five thumbs-up gestures. Interpret this as wire 5: the green wire. Cut wire 5 if your manual decoding agrees.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The system confirms that wire 5 was correct, and the bomb has changed. The new visible state is display `4`, blue light, with wire 5 already cut; the remaining wires are red, white, yellow, orange, purple, blue. Mute again sent five thumbs-up gestures, but that may be stale or may encode the next instruction, so Blind should wait for the manual-derived rule rather than assume wire 5 again.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 5 was confirmed correct and the bomb changed. New state: display 4, blue light; wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 already cut, 6 purple, 7 blue. Please decode the next required action and relay it to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 5 was confirmed correct; the bomb changed. New state: display 4, blue light; wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 already cut, 6 purple, 7 blue. Mute again signalled five thumbs-ups, but await manual confirmation before acting.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

Mute has sent three thumbs-up gestures, and the previous five-thumb signal correctly identified wire 5. The consistent encoding is therefore the wire number. In the new state, wire 3 is yellow, so Blind should cut wire 3.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent three thumbs-up gestures. Using the confirmed count-to-wire encoding, cut wire 3, the yellow wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 3 was confirmed correct, so it is now cut along with wire 5. The bomb has changed to display `7` with a purple light; the remaining wires are red, white, orange, purple, and blue. Mute’s repeated three-thumbs signal cannot safely mean wire 3 again, since that wire is already cut. I am asking Mute to decode the next action from the manual rather than sending Blind toward an already cut wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 3 was confirmed correct and is now cut. New state: display 7, purple light; wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 cut, 4 orange, 5 cut, 6 purple, 7 blue. Your three thumbs signal cannot safely mean wire 3 again. Decode the next required wire from the manual.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 3 was confirmed correct and is now cut. New state: display 7, purple light; wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 cut, 4 orange, 5 cut, 6 purple, 7 blue. Do not cut wire 3 again; await Mute's manual-derived instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute has sent one thumbs-up. The earlier signals were confirmed as wire numbers (five meant wire 5, three meant wire 3), so this indicates wire 1. The red wire is still present and should be cut next.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent one thumbs-up, indicating wire 1 under the confirmed count-to-wire encoding. Cut wire 1, the red wire.")
wait()
```

System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 1 was confirmed correct, and the bomb has changed again. The current state is display `7`, green light, with wires 1, 3, and 5 cut; wires 2 (white), 4 (orange), 6 (purple), and 7 (blue) remain. Mute’s one-thumb signal was used for the previous state, so it must not be reused to cut wire 1 again. I am giving Blind the updated state and asking for the next manual-derived instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 1 was confirmed correct and is now cut. New state: display 7, green light; wires 1, 3, and 5 cut; remaining wires 2 white, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue. Do not cut wire 1 again; await the next instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 1 was confirmed correct. New state: display 7, green light; wires 1, 3, and 5 cut; remaining wires 2 white, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue. Please decode the next required wire.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

Mute sent seven thumbs-up gestures. The confirmed encoding identifies wire 7, which is still present and blue. I am instructing Blind to cut wire 7.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent seven thumbs-up gestures, indicating wire 7. Cut wire 7, the blue wire.")
wait()
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 7 was confirmed correct and is now cut. The new state is display `3`, green light, with only wires 2 (white), 4 (orange), and 6 (purple) remaining. Mute’s repeated seven-thumb signal cannot identify a usable wire, since wire 7 is already cut; Blind should not act on it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 7 was confirmed correct and is now cut. New state: display 3, green light; remaining wires are 2 white, 4 orange, and 6 purple. Your seven-thumb signal refers to a cut wire. Please provide the next usable wire.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 7 was confirmed correct and is now cut. New state: display 3, green light; remaining wires are 2 white, 4 orange, and 6 purple. Do not cut wire 7; await a usable instruction from Mute.")
wait()
```
